'''''Vulpia myuros''''', the '''annual fescue''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=VUMY|taxon=Vulpia myuros|access-date=6 August 2015}}</ref> or '''rat's-tail fescue''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> is an annual [[flowering plant]] in grass family [[Poaceae]]. It was probably originally native to Eurasia, but it can now be found nearly worldwide as a [[introduced species|naturalized species]].

In the [[United Kingdom]] it forms dense, even swards of fine, hair-like stems in recently disturbed habitats. It is often eventually displaced by [[perennial]] grasses.

==Invasive species==
''Vulpia myuros'' is considered a [[noxious weed]] and [[invasive species]] in places where it is not native, especially in areas with a [[Mediterranean climate]].<ref name=fs>[http://www.fs.fed.us/database/feis/plants/graminoid/vulmyu/all.html US Forest Service Fire Ecology]</ref> For example, it is widespread in [[California]], where it is now a dominant species in many types of grassy habitat.<ref name=fs/>
